newsitem.title: HONG KONG: London to make statement on HK ethnic minorities.
newsitem.headline: London to make statement on HK ethnic minorities.

text.p: The British government will make a statement in parliament on Tuesday afternoon about Hong Kong's ethnic minorities, a Hong Kong government spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman said she had no information on the content of the statement, but a British newspaper earlier reported that London is expected to announce up to 8,000 mainly Indian and Pakistani Hong Kong residents can have British passports.

The prospect of British citizenship was welcomed by representatives of Hong Kong's non-Chinese residents, who face possible statelessness after the British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
"If it is true, I'm absolutely delighted," Council of Hong Kong Indian Organisations chairman K. Sital told Reuters.

The Daily Telegraph said the move was a recognition of concerns raised by Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten that non-Chinese ethnic minorities could be rendered stateless when the colony is handed back to China.
British Home Secretary Michael Howard could make the announcement as early as Tuesday with a simultaneous announcement expected in Hong Kong, the paper said.
Ethnic minority representatives have always said their community members do not want to move to Britain en masse and have every intention of remaining in Hong Kong.
Rather, they just wanted a guarantee they will not be stuck in limbo regarding nationality.
